experiment.title: AMD gsplat vs Berkelium deterministic backward on one MI300X
experiment.approval_note: Consumes MI300X credit. Set approved=true only after the owner approves the cost estimate.

semantics: All backends use profile gsplat_v1: alpha=min(0.999, o*exp(-sigma)); skip if sigma<0 or alpha<1/255; stop exclusively when T*(1-alpha)<=1e-4; eps2d=0.3; FOV-clipped Jacobian (1.3x); opacity-aware 3.33-sigma tile radius; depth-sorted per tile. Known differences: equal-depth ties are broken by Gaussian index in the reference and by sort stability in gsplat; the reference differentiates the forward with autograd (cumprod), while gsplat and Berkelium recover transmittance in backward by division (T /= 1-alpha); gsplat accumulates cross-tile gradients with float atomicAdd, Berkelium with fixed-order per-intersection reductions.

config.description: Matched AMD gsplat (atomic backward) vs Berkelium (same gsplat forward + deterministic HIP backward) on one MI300X. Same scenes, cameras, resolution, parameterization, precision (fp32), profile gsplat_v1, iteration budget. FP64 CPU reference is the oracle for correctness on the small cases only.

estimated_cost.note: estimate only; the FP64 CPU oracle dominates for the 100k case. Billing unit/rate must be checked on the provider before approval.
